newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hedges made for rally or selloff.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hedges made for rally or selloff.

text.p: Will U.S. stocks rally after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting or will they fall?
Traders of major stock index options said Wednesday investors were hedging for either move, with the only consensus expectation being a drop in volatility.
"It's 50/50," one dealer in S&P 100 .OEX and S&P 500 .SPX options said. "I hear both ways and a lot of people talking about what they're going to do this weekend."
U.S. equity markets close early Thursday and will remain closed Friday in observance of Independence Day.
But before that, traders and investors are awaiting news from the FOMC on interest rates. The policy-setting unit of the Federal Reserve met Tuesday and again Wednesday morning.
An announcement on policy is expected in early afternoon, around 1315 CDT/1815 GMT.

Few analysts, traders or economists are expecting the central bank to change rates, but some hedging in the event of a sharp market move up or down after the announcement has been seen over the last few sessions.

"I'm not expecting anything out of the ordinary, but of course we've been surprised before and it's usually right before a holiday weekend," the OEX and SPX dealer said. "I'm not on pins and needles or anything."
But investors will not be out of the woods once the FOMC meeting is over because the U.S. employment report for June is scheduled to be released Thursday before the market opens.
So despite the possibility of a drop in volatility after the FOMC announcement, the real drop is not likely to be seen until Thursday, traders said.
"I think we see what comes out of the Fed and then we touch off the numbers tomorrow," the dealer said. "It'll be an interesting morning."
Volatility in the options has to come in, he said, adding "it can't go much higher."
Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said that with S&P 500 futures trading in a tight 4.25-point range through Wednesday morning, volatility had already begun to dry up.
The volatility index .VIX, for example, was down 0.56, or 2.40 percent, at 22.82 at about 1135 CDT/1635 GMT. The index is priced off certain OEX contracts.
At the same time, September S&P 500 futures were up 0.75 at 902, having traded between 899.75 and 904.
The spot SPX index was ahead 2.85 at 893.88 and the OEX rose two to 870.37.
The blue chip Dow industrial average .DJI, meanwhile, was down nearly 19 points at about 7,704.
